title: Sabrent Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger Quick Look
gist: ServeTheHome's quick look at the Sabrent Voltik 252W desktop charger (model AX-8PTC): four 100W-rated USB-C and four 18W USB-A ports sharing a 252W total budget, with direct AC input, a per-port telemetry LCD and a mounting plate. It is useful for consolidating chargers, but it cannot power notebooks that pull more than 100W over USB-C.

themes.theme: Port layout and shared power budget

insights.claim: The Sabrent Voltik 252W desktop charging station offers four USB-C ports rated up to 100W each and four USB-A ports rated up to 18W each, with 252W of total combined output.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: This class of high-port-count USB PD desktop charger now reaches the 250W range, so laptops, phones and peripherals can all charge from one unit.
insights.locator: The USB-C ports are arranged in two rows of two

insights.claim: The Sabrent Voltik 252W's 252W rating is a shared budget, so its four USB-C ports cannot all deliver their 100W maximum at the same time.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: When judging multi-port chargers, look at how power is split across ports when several are busy, not only at the per-port peak or the headline total.
insights.quote: the four USB-C ports cannot all deliver 100W at the same time
insights.locator: The USB-C ports are arranged in two rows of two

insights.claim: The Sabrent Voltik 252W supports the USB PD 3.0, PPS, Qualcomm Quick Charge 4.0 and Quick Charge 3.0 fast-charging protocols.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Supporting several protocols is now a standard feature for desktop chargers that must work with mixed device fleets.
insights.locator: Sabrent lists support for PD 3.0, PPS, QC 4.0, and QC 3.0

insights.claim: The Sabrent Voltik 252W has an LCD that cycles through each port to show its current wattage, voltage, amperage and internal temperature, a feature STH considers valuable for its readers.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Per-port power telemetry is becoming a selling point for chargers aimed at technical and prosumer buyers.
insights.quote: Other chargers do that, but if you do not have something like that yet, then it is something that if you read STH, you will like.
insights.locator: Here is a shot of the LCD lit up

insights.claim: The Sabrent Voltik 252W (model AX-8PTC) takes AC power directly through an inlet instead of an external power brick, and ships with a mounting plate, so it is designed as a fixed desk or mounted station rather than a travel charger.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: The product is aimed at fixed workspace use, not the compact GaN travel-charger segment.
insights.quote: It is nice that the unit directly takes AC power rather than through an external power brick.
insights.locator: The power-input panel has the AC inlet

insights.claim: Some notebooks draw more than 100W over USB Type-C, so even a 252W multi-port charger with 100W-per-port limits cannot fully charge every laptop.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Laptop power draw is rising past the 100W per-port ceiling, so watch for chargers with higher per-port output to cover high-end notebooks.
insights.quote: notebooks that draw over 100W via USB Type-C

insights.claim: ServeTheHome now uses four Sabrent Voltik 252W charging stations because they replace several separate adapters with one station that has eight ports and per-port power feedback.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Buying several units shows real practical demand for consolidated desktop charging among technical users.
insights.quote: We now have four of these.
insights.locator: For a desk with several devices
